StringWithMarkup.String: 2-Propionic acid, 2-methyl, 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl ester (silane A-174) was evaluated for the ability to increase the incidence of micronucleated polychromatic erythrocytes in peripheral blood samples of male and female Swiss-Webster mice treated by I.P. injection. Groups of 10 mice (5 male and 5 female) received a single dose of 2500, 4000, 5000 mg/kg body weight of test article in corn oil; blood samples were drawn 30, 48 and 72 hours after injection. A statistically significant increase in the incidence of micronucleated polychromatic erythrocytes was not observed (Fischer exact test, p > 0.001) at any dose level or time of sampling. A statistically significant (linear regression analysis, r = -0.97) dose related decrease in the PCE/NCE ratio was observed at the 72 hour sampling time (all doses), reflecting the toxic effect of the test article. Additionally, in a preliminary toxicity test, administration of 5000 mg/kg test article (maximum testable dose) induced a 25% decrease in the polychromatic to normochromatic erythrocyte (PCE/NCE) ratio, while mortality was not observed at doses up to and including this level.

StringWithMarkup.String: The frequency of chromosomal aberrations was determined in Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells exposed to 2-propionic acid, 2-methyl, 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl ester (silane A-174) with and without metabolic activation provided by Aroclor-induced rat liver S9 fraction. CHO-K1-BH4 cells were exposed to test article at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 0.6 mg/ml in the presence and absence of activation, and samples were withdrawn at 8 and 12 hours for evaluation. In activated tests, statistically significant (Fischer's exact test, p < 0.05) increases in the incidences of aberrations were observed in samples withdrawn at 8 hours from cultures exposed to 0.3, 0.4, and 0.6 mg/ml, and in samples withdrawn at 12 hours from cultures exposed to 0.2 and 0.3 mg/ml. Additionally, it was reported that the frequency of sister chromatid exchange was increased in the 12 hour samples . A statistically significant (p < 0.01) increase in the incidence of aberrations was observed in samples withdrawn at 8 hours from nonactivated cultures exposed to 0.4 mg/ml. StringWithMarkup.String: Trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate's production and use as an adhesion or coupling agent to dental porcelain, ceramic, or glass surfaces may result in its release to the environment through various waste streams. If released to air, an estimated vapor pressure of 0.44 mm Hg at 25 °C indicates trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate will exist solely as a vapor in the atmosphere. Vapor-phase trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate will be degraded in the atmosphere by reaction with photochemically-produced hydroxyl radicals; the half-life for this reaction in air is estimated to be 15 hours. The atmospheric half-life for the vapor-phase reaction of trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate with ozone has been estimated as 24 hours. Trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate does not contain chromophores that absorb at wavelengths >290 nm and therefore is not expected to be susceptible to direct photolysis by sunlight. If released to soil, trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate is expected to have low mobility based upon an estimated Koc of 1,700. Volatilization from moist soil surfaces is not expected to be an important fate process based upon an estimated Henry's Law constant of 3.0X10-7 atm-cu m/mole. Trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate is not expected to volatilize from dry soil surfaces based upon its vapor pressure. Biodegradation data were not available. If released into water, trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate is expected to adsorb to suspended solids and sediment based upon the estimated Koc. Volatilization from water surfaces is not expected to be an important fate process based upon this compound's estimated Henry's Law constant. An estimated BCF of 3.2 suggests the potential for bioconcentration in aquatic organisms is low.  The hydrolysis of 3-methacryloxypropyl-trimethodxysilane proceeds within a few minutes in a low pH environment as a result of the catalytic action of H+ ions. A base-catalyzed second-order hydrolysis rate constant of 2.7X10-3 L/mole-sec was estimated using a structure estimation method; this corresponds to half-lives of 81 and 8.1 years at pH values of 7 and 8, respectively. Occupational exposure to trimethoxysilylpropyl methacrylate may occur through inhalation and dermal contact with this compound at workplaces where trimethoxysilylpropyl  methacrylate is produced or used. Section.Description: Sorption to soils and sediments is an important factor on the transport and fate of organic contaminants in the environment.  The soil/water adsorption coefficient, also known as solid-water distribution coefficient (Kd), measures the amount of chemical substance adsorbed onto soil per amount of water.  Since adsorption occurs predominantly by partition into the soil organic matter, it is more useful to normalize the Kd value to the organic carbon content of a soil and express the distribution coefficient in Koc (organic carbon normalized distribution coefficient).  The greater the Kd (or Koc) value, the less likely a chemical will leach or contribute to runoff.  A very high value means it is strongly adsorbed onto soil and organic matter and does not move throughout the soil.
